text:
Leah (Sales): ACME security hit back with a few CAIQ redlines focused on KMS/HSM and key rotation. they want a short bundle we can paste into the CAIQ and the contract.
Evan (SecEng): paste the exact asks?
Leah (Sales): 1) proof HSM-backed keys are supported, 2) do you allow customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for hosted instances, 3) who rotates keys and frequency, 4) can Redwood access customer keys for recovery, 5) transport/in-transit protection.
Priya (Solutions): TL;DR for CAIQ: AES-256 envelope encryption for data at rest, per-tenant data keys encrypted by a wrapping key, support for customer-managed KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) and KMIP HSMs for Private/Dedicated. HSM attestation docs available pre-POC.
Noah (Infra): Implementation detail: Hosted BYOK - we integrate via cloud KMS APIs and never import plaintext root keys. For Private, you can point to your KMIP endpoint or provide a wrapped key. We support HSMs (nShield/CloudHSM/Thales) with FIPS 140-2/3 validated modules.
Evan (SecEng): On the "who rotates" question: if customer uses BYOK, rotation is controlled by customer KMS and Redwood will honor new wrapping keys via the configured integration. If using Redwood-managed KMS, default rolling policy: wrapping key rotate every 180 days (configurable), data keys rotated/rewrapped automatically as we perform background rewraps. For high-security customers we recommend 90-day wrapping key rotation.
ClientRep (ACME): do you ever escrow keys or hold plaintext for emergency access? that's a blocker for us.
Priya (Solutions): we do not escrow customer root keys. For Hosted BYOK flow, keys remain in the customer's KMS or are uploaded as a wrapped key; Redwood does not store plaintext/unwrapped key material. For Redwood-managed keys, we control the wrapping key and can provide documented emergency access procedures under contract (with dual-approval and audit logging).
Evan (SecEng): Add audit controls: all key operations are logged to immutable audit trails (timestamp, actor, operation, request id). Logs can be exported to customer SIEM for Dedicated/Private.
Noah (Infra): In-transit: TLS 1.2+ mandatory, TLS 1.3 preferred, strong cipher suites (AES-GCM, ECDHE), mutual TLS available for Private. We never transmit customer key material outside the configured KMS boundary in plaintext.
Leah (Sales): good. legal also wants sample contract language we can paste. can you write a 1-2 sentence blurb?
Evan (SecEng): "Redwood protects data at rest using AES-256-GCM with an envelope encryption scheme. Customers may provide and manage their own wrapping keys via supported KMS integrations (BYOK); HSM-backed keys are supported and meet FIPS 140-2/3 requirements. Redwood does not export customer key material in plaintext and maintains audit logs of key access."
ClientRep (ACME): perfect. also asking for POC checklist: what will you demo to show we retain key control?
Priya (Solutions): POC checklist: 1) stand up Dedicated/VPC POC or Private trial, 2) configure customer KMS key/ARN or KMIP endpoint, 3) run sample ingest and verify ciphertext in storage, 4) rotate wrapping key in customer KMS and show seamless rewrap (no downtime), 5) produce HSM attestation + cert chain, 6) export audit logs to our S3/Splunk sample.
Noah (Infra): I'll prepare a temporary attestation PDF and upload to secure link prior to the call. also can show live CloudHSM key id and the KMS describe-key output.
Leah (Sales): toss in a small example command for the CAIQ response so they see it's standard.
Priya (Solutions): example snippet:
```bash
# verify key exists in customer AWS KMS before configuring Redwood
aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/acme-redwood-poc --profile acme-prod
# Redwood will reference the key ARN and never receive plaintext key material
```
ClientRep (ACME): thanks. timeline: can you deliver attestation and the CAIQ answers by Tue COB?
Noah (Infra): yes, attestation upload ETA Mon evening. will post secure link here.
UploadBot: attestation-upload: https://redwood-secure.s3/attestations/acme-poc-hsm-attest.pdf (expires in 7d) :lock: :white_check_mark:
Leah (Sales): awesome. I'm going to paste Evan's contract snippet + the POC checklist into the CAIQ responses and send to legal. ping me if we need to tighten any language. :rocket:
